user_intent: Land a minimal meta-governed fix for the edit-plan anchor placement ambiguity exposed by real-provider testing.
title: Align edit-plan anchor contract for real-provider output
description: A real-provider E2E probe showed that one provider placed replace_anchor anchor text under target.anchor while the current compiler only accepts top-level edit.anchor. This request records an owner-requested meta iteration to clarify the canonical contract and add bounded compiler compatibility without changing approval, apply, provider, or workflow authority.
expected_artifacts: Patch Compiler anchor accessor that keeps top-level edit.anchor canonical while accepting target.anchor as a compatibility alias when unambiguous
Implementation Agent prompt clarification and replace_anchor example showing top-level anchor
Regression tests for target.anchor compatibility, canonical top-level anchor support, and conflicting anchor rejection
Validation results from targeted pytest, full pytest, compileall, and abyss_cli check

request_fields.activation_policy: delayed; candidate material only until owner review and normal ChangeSet boundaries; no same-cycle activation of any governance rule change
request_fields.affected_governance_surface: Self Evolution edit-plan contract, Implementation Agent output contract, and Patch Compiler validation boundary. This changes field parsing compatibility for anchor-based edit plans but does not change approval, apply, dry-run, provider, path, or owner-authority policy.
request_fields.current_problem: The Implementation Agent prompt mentions target.path and symbol or anchor but only shows a replace_symbol example. The compiler reads edit.get('anchor') for replace_anchor and append_after_anchor, so a reasonable target.anchor placement from a real provider fails with EDIT_PLAN_CONTRACT_MISSING_ANCHOR even though the output is otherwise structurally valid.
request_fields.owner_authority_impact: No reduction or delegation of Owner authority. Real-provider test success remains evidence only and does not approve, apply, commit, or activate changes. Existing Owner approval gates remain unchanged.
request_fields.old_rule_review: Prior rules require changes touching agent contracts or self-iteration validation boundaries to be recorded before modification. Existing governance forbids bypassing proposal, dry-run, Harness review, Owner approval, and apply gates. This request preserves those gates and only aligns edit-plan field parsing/documentation.
request_fields.risk_assessment: Main risk is accepting an additional anchor location. Mitigation: top-level edit.anchor remains canonical, target.anchor is accepted only as an alias when top-level anchor is absent or equal, both still require unique exact anchor resolution, and conflicting anchors are explicitly rejected.
request_fields.rollback_plan: Revert the anchor accessor and call-site changes in abyss_cli/patch_compiler.py, revert the Implementation Agent prompt clarification/example, and remove the added regression tests. Existing top-level anchor edit plans continue to work without this compatibility alias.
request_fields.validation_plan: Run targeted edit-plan compiler tests, compileall, full pytest, and abyss_cli check. Confirm target.anchor compiles, conflicting anchors are rejected, and canonical top-level anchor remains supported.
request_fields.proposed_change: Keep top-level edit.anchor as the canonical contract; explicitly document that target must contain path only; add a replace_anchor example; make the compiler accept target.anchor as a compatibility alias when top-level anchor is absent. If both top-level anchor and target.anchor are present and differ, reject the plan with an explicit conflicting-anchor contract error.
